subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt/rebase the open conflicting fork PR or close/supersede it and queue a fresh narrow same-repo fix for the session-title metadata bug?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but an open fork PR with closing syntax already claims the fix and is currently conflicting, so automation should not create a competing fix until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the stale conflicting fork PR and land a focused same-repo fix with metadata stripping, display metadata precedence, and regression coverage.

options.title: Adopt/Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer or contributor update the open fork PR against current main and add real TUI/Gateway proof before review.

options.title: Keep Waiting On Fork PR
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the open fork branch despite its conflict state and lack of recent activity.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the stale conflicting fork PR and land a focused same-repo fix with metadata stripping, display metadata precedence, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is tied to the original title-picker commits and the later transcript-field caching work that shapes the safest fix boundary.
